name: Battle of Badr
note: The accounts do not say where each Muslim battalion stood or how the Meccan army was drawn up, so the two Muslim battalions are placed side by side and the Meccans as one body. The sizes of the blocks are by judgement. The Meccan army is given as around 1300 men, and also as nearly one thousand strong. The Muslim tradition holds that angels were sent to strengthen the Muslims and terrify the Quraysh, as the Qur'an states; the plan shows only the movements of the men.

terrain.name: al-Asfal Mountain
terrain.quote: The west of the valley was covered by the al-Asfal Mountain

terrain.name: Sand dunes
terrain.quote: The valley of Badr is surrounded by two large sand dunes to the east

terrain.name: Date-palms
terrain.quote: Muhammad and his army had encamped at some date-palms in the north

terrain.name: Well
terrain.quote: They had taken a well near the center of the western margin of al-'Udwatul Dunya

terrain.name: Road from Mecca
terrain.quote: which was the primary route from Mecca

units.quote: one of the 82 Muhajirun and the other of the 231 Ansar

units.quote: one of the 82 Muhajirun and the other of the 231 Ansar

units.name: Muslim duellists
units.quote: Hamza approached and called on Ubayda ibn al-Harith and Ali ibn Abi Talib to join him

units.name: Meccan champion al-Aswad
units.quote: al-Aswad ibn Abd al-Asad, one of the men from Abu Jahl's clan, the Banu Makhzum

units.name: Meccan army
units.quote: an excited army of around 1300 men, 100 horses and a large number of camels

units.name: Meccan duellists
units.quote: Utba ibn Rabi'a, alongside his brother, Shayba ibn Rabi'a and son, al-Walid ibn Utba, emerged from the Meccan ranks

phases.title: The armies face each other across the valley
phases.text: The Quraysh were encamped in the south-eastern part of the valley near the road from Mecca. The Muslims had come from the north and held the well nearest the Meccans.
phases.quote: The Quraysh had encamped in the south-eastern portion of the valley near the road to Mecca, while Muhammad and his army had encamped at some date-palms in the north.

phases.title: Al-Aswad challenges for the well
phases.text: Al-Aswad, a man of Abu Jahl's clan, swore to drink from the Muslims' well or destroy it or die for it. Hamza came out and fought him. Hamza struck his leg and then dealt a second blow that killed him.
phases.quote: In response to his cries, Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib, one of Muhammad's uncles, came out and they began fighting in a duel.

phases.title: Three Meccans challenge and are answered
phases.text: Utba, his brother Shayba and his son al-Walid came out of the Meccan ranks. Hamza, Ubayda and Ali went out to meet them. Ali killed al-Walid and Hamza killed Shayba, while Ubayda was seriously wounded.
phases.quote: The first two duels between Ali and al-Walid and Hamza and Shayba were quick with both managing to kill their opponents swiftly.

phases.title: Ubayda is carried back to the Muslim lines
phases.text: Hamza found Ubayda seriously wounded after the fight between Ali and al-Walid. Ali and Hamza then carried him back into the Muslim lines.
phases.quote: Ali and Hamza then carried Ubayda back into the Muslim lines.

phases.title: The Meccans charge
phases.text: A shower of arrows from both sides followed the duels. The Meccans then took the offensive and charged upon the Muslim lines, and the Muslim duellists were carried back into the lines.
phases.quote: A shower of arrows from both sides followed these duels and this was followed by several other duels, most of which were won by the Muslims. The Meccans now took the offensive and charged upon the Muslim lines.

phases.title: The Muslims counter-attack
phases.text: Muhammad gave the order for a counter-attack and the Muslim army rushed the Quraysh lines. Both Muslim battalions moved forward against the Meccan body.
phases.quote: Muhammad gave the order to carry out a counterattack against the enemy now

phases.title: The Meccan lines break
phases.text: The Meccans broke and ran. The fighting lasted a few hours and was over by early afternoon, after the Meccan army had scattered.
phases.quote: The Meccans, understrength and unenthusiastic about fighting, promptly broke and ran.
